Design the relational schema with proper keys and indexes, denormalized counters (post count, last post time and author on the thread) maintained transactionally, and soft deletion for moderation. Implement endpoints for creating threads and replies, listing threads in a category with keyset pagination by last activity, and paging through posts in a thread. Store passwords properly hashed, not in plain varchar, and add tests plus a seed script that generates a large forum to check query plans.

generic_title: Store the app's models append-only with versions
generic_prompt: In this FastAPI service, I want some models stored append-only: rows are never updated or deleted. Every change inserts a new row with the same id and an incremented version, and deleting inserts a new version with is_deleted set. Implement this at the data layer so the rest of the code keeps calling normal save and delete methods: a composite (id, version) key, a view or query helper that returns only the latest non-deleted version of each record, a uniqueness guarantee so two concurrent writers can't create the same version, and endpoints to fetch an item's history and its state at a point in time. Add indexes that keep 'current version' reads fast and tests for concurrent updates.
title: Store reminder lists and items append-only with history
prompt: In this reminders web app (FastAPI with Jinja and HTMX, a JSON API, and Playwright tests), lists and items live in a single JSON file and every edit overwrites the old data. Move them into a relational database stored append-only: renaming a list, editing, completing or deleting an item inserts a new row with the same id and an incremented version (deletes set is_deleted), and nothing is ever updated in place. Keep the existing routes and HTMX partials working through a repository that returns only the latest non-deleted versions, guarantee concurrent edits can't create the same version, and add API endpoints to view an item's history and a list as it was at a given time. Include a migration from the JSON file and tests.

generic_title: Audit-log raw request and response bodies without slowing responses
generic_prompt: In this FastAPI service, which will run in a container orchestrator, we need an audit trail: for every API route, capture the raw JSON request body and the JSON response body, together with method, path, status code, timestamp and duration, and ship them to a durable log/audit store. Bodies are small (a few KB). Logging must not add noticeable latency, so write the audit records asynchronously (off the request path) rather than inline. Ensure streaming responses still work and the body can still be read by the route handler after the middleware reads it.
title: Audit-log raw request and response bodies for the shop API
prompt: In this e-commerce shop API, compliance wants an audit trail of every call to the product, account and order-related routes: capture the raw JSON request body and JSON response body along with method, path, status code, authenticated user (if any), timestamp and duration, and ship each record to a durable log/audit store. Bodies are small. Auditing must not noticeably slow responses, so emit the records asynchronously off the request path. Mask secrets such as passwords and OTP codes before they are logged, and ensure file uploads for product media are not dumped into the audit log.

generic_title: Add low-overhead request metrics to a model-serving API

Our previous instrumentation middleware added latency under load and the metrics endpoint starved under ~4 req/s, causing some requests to time out. Choose an approach that keeps per-request overhead minimal, works with multiple worker processes, and keeps the metrics endpoint responsive under load.
title: Add low-overhead request metrics to the reminders app

Also count business events such as reminder lists and items created or completed. Keep per-request overhead minimal, make it work if the app runs with multiple worker processes, and ensure the metrics endpoint stays responsive under load.

title: Emit structured JSON logs for the todo API

The server's own startup and access logs must use the same format as our module loggers, with no duplicate lines, and sensitive data (passwords, verification and password-reset tokens) must never appear in logs.

Waiting for the result must never block the event loop. Run the worker as a separate process, retry transient failures, and record failures so the user sees a clear error.
